sampling_model.design: Independent regime samples with fixed reference law \(\mu_0\) and known compact supports.
sampling_model.units: For every \(p\in\mathcal A\), observe \(Y_{p,1},\ldots,Y_{p,n_p}\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}P_p\), independently across regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: The regime label indexes an interventional law or a conditionally identified law; the common-rank equation fixes the same-unit coupling.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-propensity overlap is needed after the regime laws are identified; density nondegeneracy is \(b\le f_p\le B\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Project the density at \(k_n\), use the positive fallback off the regularity event, solve Monge--Ampere, smooth the potential at \(h_n\), form \(\widetilde H_p\), and spectrally clip at \(m/4\) before every inverse and margin statistic. Beyond the simultaneous-band threshold clipping is inactive; for a negative margin endpoint, an additional eventual-radius comparison verifies the distinct source-product trigger before the validated certificate branch is run.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 5.3 states that there is no precise characterization of structural causal models inducing cyclically monotone counterfactuals.

Section 3.1, Definition 1 and equation (6), together with Theorem 2, show that invertible cyclically comonotone production functions make \(h_1\circ h_0^{-1}\) the Brenier natural-trend map and identify the treated counterfactual distribution by its pushforward.

NeurIPS Theorem 4.12, repeated as Appendix Theorem B.11 in equations (13) and (72), claims strict Euclidean monotonicity for time-one dynamic optimal-transport counterfactual maps under a uniform-cube Markovian source and Lemma 4.6/B.5 regularity.
Theorem 2.1 represents conditional vector quantiles as gradients of convex functions from a common absolutely continuous reference law.
The paper proves pointwise central limit theorems for smooth plug-in Brenier maps on a flat torus and rules out global weak convergence in high dimension.
Theorems 1 and 2 establish near-matching minimax integrated squared-error rates for smooth optimal-transport map estimation.
Theorems 1.3 and 1.5 give global potential stability and characterize the conormal linear response along smooth density paths.

body.tldr: Separate Brenier structure does not guarantee that a same-unit counterfactual composition preserves Euclidean ranks. The exact population frontier and sharp margin \(\gamma_{pq}\) are paired with a two-resolution estimator whose reported Hessian is deterministically clipped at \(m/4\), so every inverse and statistic exists; the simultaneous-band theorem makes clipping inactive beyond its threshold. In that eventual-radius regime, a negative margin-band endpoint quantitatively implies the distinct source-product trigger used by the validated interval search, which then returns a rational violating chord and population-increment enclosures. No equivalence of the two triggers is claimed at arbitrary radii. The conditional upper rate is \((\log n/n)^{s/(2s+d)}\), while an explicit common-support quadratic-bump family proves the matching lower separation rate independently of the endpoint-response question.

project_justification.gap: Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024), Section 3.1, Definition 1 and Theorem 2, identify a nonlinear difference-in-differences counterfactual law when \(h_0,h_1\) are cyclically comonotone, but do not give a pointwise symmetric-cross-Hessian if-and-only-if Euclidean frontier, the Hessian-commutation if-and-only-if cyclic-gradient frontier, the sharp global margin, or inference for that margin. Their causal composition framework and the common-rank Brenier framework are incomparable: they allow cyclically comonotone production functions that need not individually be cyclic gradients, whereas the noncommuting pair \(A_0,A_1\) and an open neighborhood around it are individually Brenier but fail cyclical comonotonicity. Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker's displayed dynamic-transport conditions likewise admit this open-neighborhood pair although its symmetric cross-Hessian is indefinite. Current statistical optimal-transport theory estimates map values in integrated loss or gives pointwise limits; it does not provide honest inference for a global derivative-level cross-regime eigenvalue margin, nor a terminating validated chord certificate whose source-product trigger is quantitatively linked to a negative margin endpoint.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a population-and-sampling frontier for Euclidean same-unit rank preservation within the smooth common-rank Brenier class: an exact algebraic criterion, an observable scalar margin, and, beyond the band theorem's eventual-radius threshold, a reproducible failure witness produced through a distinct source-product inequality. This is separate from nonlinear difference-in-differences identification, and it does not claim the counterfactual-law or treatment-effect identification results of Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet.
project_justification.fill: The symmetric cross-Hessian theorem characterizes Euclidean monotonicity, and the commutation theorem characterizes exactly the cyclic-gradient subfamily; within the common-rank Brenier class, Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet's cyclical-comonotonicity implication corresponds to this commuting subfamily rather than the full class. The open-neighborhood matrices \(A_0,A_1\) separate both that subfamily and Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker's claimed implication. The inference layer uses an everywhere-valid positive density fallback and \(m/4\) spectral clipping, proves clipping inactive on the simultaneous band beyond its threshold, and tracks the selected resolutions and endpoint logarithm in an explicit Hessian envelope. After enlarging the threshold so the deterministic radius is sufficiently small, a congruence bound proves that \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}+w_n<0\) implies the different source-product trigger with allowance \((2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}\); only then does the validated search return a rational violating chord. A named transversal matrix path and localized quadratic bumps preserve every support and model restriction with slack, place every mixture component in the composite null, and deliver the unconditional lower rate through Le Cam's \(\chi^2\) mixture bound without using the endpoint-response OEQ.

body.related_work: De Lara and Ganassali (2025), Section 5.3, leave the cyclically monotone SCM characterization unresolved. Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024), Section 3.1, Definition 1 and equation (6), define cyclical comonotonicity and show immediately afterward that it makes \(h_1\circ h_0^{-1}\) cyclically monotone; Theorem 2 uses that condition in a nonlinear difference-in-differences model to identify the treated counterfactual law. The same subsection explicitly notes that a composition of optimal-transport maps is generally not itself an optimal transport except in special circumstances. Their framework does not supply the pointwise symmetric-cross-Hessian if-and-only-if Euclidean frontier, the Hessian-commutation if-and-only-if cyclic-gradient frontier, the sharp global margin, or its inference. Conversely, the common-rank Brenier framework does not claim their nonlinear difference-in-differences identification result. The two model classes are strictly incomparable: Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet allow cyclically comonotone production functions that need not individually be cyclic gradients, while this project requires every regime map to be a Brenier gradient; in the other direction, the noncommuting \(A_0,A_1\) pair and its open SPD neighborhood consist of individual Brenier maps but are not cyclically comonotone because their inverse composition is not cyclically monotone. Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker (NeurIPS 2025), Theorem 4.12 and Appendix Theorem B.11, state strict Euclidean monotonicity in equations (13) and (72) under a uniform-cube Markovian source and Lemma 4.6/B.5 dynamic-OT regularity; their proof at equations (79)--(86) uses a state-dependent weighted inner product. The same open-neighborhood pair satisfies their displayed assumptions while its symmetric cross-Hessian is indefinite, so those assumptions do not imply the Euclidean frontier; this project does not claim their dynamic or Markovian identification results. Carlier, Chernozhukov, and Galichon (2016), Theorem 2.1, supply common-reference vector quantiles, not inverse-composition geometry. Hutter and Rigollet (2021) give integrated map-risk rates. Manole et al. (2024) provide plug-in and boundary-wavelet machinery, while Manole et al. (2023) give pointwise torus limits rather than global Hessian bands. Ghosal and Sen (2022) study rank maps, not cross-Hessian margins. Caja-Lopez, Delgadino, and Kitagawa (2026), Theorems 1.3--1.5, provide conormal response and lower-derivative stability. Dong, Lee, and Kim (2018), Theorems 1.7 and 1.10, provide the boundary Dini template. Chen and Fang (2019) motivates avoiding an ordinary bootstrap claim at a degenerate nonsmooth functional. None of these works supplies the validated source-product interval search here, and this note distinguishes that search's separate sufficient trigger from the scalar statistical margin event except where the eventual-radius congruence argument proves the implication.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The raw Hessian response is order zero and incurs logarithmic accumulation; signed high-order smoothing also need not preserve positive definiteness. The reported field therefore clips eigenvalues at \(m/4\). This is only a totalization device: the simultaneous-band theorem makes clipping inactive on \(\mathcal B_n\) after its sample threshold. The finite certificate additionally uses a source-product trigger with scalar perturbation allowance \((2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2\). A negative margin endpoint implies that trigger only after enlarging the threshold so \(r_{H,n}\) is sufficiently small; the triggers are not asserted equivalent at arbitrary radii. Validated interval arithmetic is essential, since arbitrary floating-point PDE output is not self-validating. The minimax converse is restricted to nondegenerate class constants containing the displayed quadratic path with strict slack; degenerate constant choices can collapse the testing problem.
body.honest_scope: The structural frontiers, NeurIPS-assumption-aligned witness, two-resolution decomposition, clipping-inactivity implication, explicit fixed-support Le Cam lower family, and eventual-radius validated certificate are theorem targets. The boundary-uniform endpoint estimate and quadratic remainder are open. Only the upper band, upper separation rate, and certificate implication from the negative margin endpoint depend on the affirmative endpoint-response premise and its band threshold; the lower separation bound does not. The certificate algorithm's primitive source-product trigger is a distinct sufficient condition; outside the proved eventual-radius comparison, no implication or equivalence with the statistical margin endpoint is claimed, and termination is not promised at zero margin. The lower theorem applies exactly to nondegenerate choices of the existing class constants admitting the displayed strict-slack quadratic path; this is a nonvacuity qualification, not an added assumption. No adaptation, irregular-support, coordinate-invariance, zero-margin certification, or unvalidated-numerics claim is made. The scalar and simultaneously diagonal cases reduce to ordinary positive derivative ratios.
